blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Before his death on Wednesday, Oct. 7, “Tatay” Elmer Cordero had spent the last years of his life fighting battles bigger than himself — for his livelihood, for drivers like him and, most of all, for what he believed ordinary Filipinos were entitled to demand from their government. For many, Cordero first came into public view in 2020, when a photograph of the elderly jeepney driver in detention became a symbol of the struggles faced by transport workers at the height of the Covid-19 pandemic, which claimed not only lives but livelihoods.
